## Why This Is Asked

This tests end-to-end upgrade governance at scale: enforcing tenant isolation, cross-cluster canaries, and SBOM-based gates in production.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-cluster Argo Rollouts canary strategies
- OPA/Kyverno style policies for time-window upgrades
- SBOM integrity checks as upgrade gates
- Tenant isolation via SPIFFE IDs
- Central audit webhook for traceability

## Code Example
```yaml
# Argo Rollouts canary manifest (minimal)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-rollout
spec:
  replicas: 2
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: cnf
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 300s }
```

```yaml
# Audit webhook payload (example)
tenant: tenant-A
upgrade: cnf-service:1.2.3
cluster: eu-west-1
status: canary
timestamp: 2026-01-31T12:34:56Z
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the policy windows and canary gates in a multi-tenant sandbox?
- What metrics and alerting would you rely on for automatic rollback?

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.canary
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  enabled: "true"
  target: "/v1/foo"
```
```yaml
# Sidecar snippet (pseudo)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-sidecar
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sidecar
        image: cnf/sidecar:latest
        env:
        - name: CANARY_ENABLED
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.canary
              key: enabled
        - name: CANARY_TARGET
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.canary
              key: target
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy-as-code proficiency, practical use of Gatekeeper/OPA, and ability to derive concrete manifests and validation steps for a CNF multi-tenant setup.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, hostNetwork, and Privileged security controls
- Namespace-scoped policy targeting CNFs
- Lightweight test manifests to validate allow/deny paths

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: cnfnamespacesecurity.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: cnf-a-security
spec:
  namespace: cnf-a
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-cnf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      privileged: false
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# Non-compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-cnf
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      privileged: true
```

## Follow-up Steps

- Apply ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, and test manifests in a single namespace and observe denial events for non-compliant pods.
- Extend with a quick kubectl patch to simulate remediation and re-validate.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of per-tenant security in a CNF gateway using Kubernetes Secrets and sidecars. It also probes how to validate signatures without leaking keys and how to handle clock skew.

## Key Concepts
- HMAC-SHA256 signatures, per-tenant secrets, sidecar interception
- Kubernetes Secrets, volume mounts, reload on secret update
- Retry/deny logic via HTTP 401, clock skew handling
- End-to-end test using a minimal manifest

## Code Example
```javascript
function verify(req, secret) {
  const msg = req.method + '|' + req.path + '|' + req.headers['X-TIMESTAMP'];
  const sig = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(msg).digest('hex');
  return req.headers['X-Signature'] === sig;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate keys and propagate new secrets without downtime?
- How can you mitigate replay attacks beyond timestamp checks?
